lines.text: intelligence is a property of the medium, not the agent
lines.note: the brainless network still needs a brain to place the emission centers: the attractor geometry decides every network the colony could possibly grow, so the mold never solves the maze — it answers the question the anchors asked.

note_src.quote: critical_parameter: emission_centers layout — the attractor geometry determines every possible network the colony can grow

lines.text: purpose is not inside the agent — it lives in the field the agent inhabits
lines.note: the whole decision is a lookup — one arrow at one grid cell — so purpose sits wherever the drawing puts it: arrows shown, a diagram of a cause; arrows hidden, the same agents look like they want something.

note_src.quote: With arrows the piece is a diagram of a cause; with them hidden the agents look like they want something. Same simulation, opposite claim about where purpose lives.

lines.text: Change one relation; watch a local arrow and the flock together.
Emergent flocking behavior simulation using Craig Reynolds' boids algorithm
lines.note: three rules make the school and a fourth holds it — the glass: separation, alignment and cohesion bound no volume, so the tank is the only truly external rule and the flock you can watch is a captivity effect.

note_src.quote: the boundary of the tank is the only rule that is truly external — every other behavior is the boids talking to each other

lines.text: coordination is not agreement — it is geometry
Ant colony optimization with pheromone evaporation gradient heatmap
lines.note: the crowd surprises only because each agent was made legible first — exploring, gathering, fleeing, returning — since a match on agent state cannot branch unless a life compresses to a label, so the whole's opacity is bought with the part's.

note_src.quote: The `match agent["state"]` block requires that the agent's condition be compressible into a label.

lines.text: the map is written by the travelers — the territory and the route emerge together
lines.note: the colony writes its own map but cannot choose the paper: the emission centers stand before the first ant walks, so every trail it finds is an answer to a geometry no traveler set.

note_src.quote: The colony writes its own map. What it CANNOT choose is the shape of the problem: where the fixed points are.

pearls.edge: the meeting stays a meeting only because the room forces reynolds on both sides: neither flock can overwrite the other, only respond — let one side be a point target and the chamber becomes a hunt.

edge_src.quote: a chamber that let one side be a swarm and the other be a point target would be a chamber about hunting a swarm

lines.text: order is not imposed from outside — it falls into existence when local interactions exceed the noise …
lines.note: self-organised order still descends a valley someone built: the fitness function was picked by a programmer who knew the minimum before the first particle moved — the swarm is scored against an answer it cannot question.

note_src.quote: But the valley was constructed. The fitness function was chosen — Rastrigin, Ackley, Rosenbrock — by a programmer who knew the answer before the particles started searching.

lines.text: A remembered position remains; its claim to be best must be scored again.
evolution has no goal — only the dead are wrong, and only the living get to try again
lines.note: Local events and population-scale interventions coexist. The live care record identifies restocking, predator pressure and supplied food; it does not claim what removing them would cause.
